His response was dismissive, stating that if chemists don’t recognize these medicines, they shouldn’t be working there.

This is not the first time I’ve faced this issue with the same doctor, which is why I had made the request in advance. This kind of practice feels inconvenient and raises concerns about transparency and patient-first care.

owner_posts.post_text: In a world that moves fast, yoga reminds us to slow down, breathe, and reconnect with ourselves.

A patient came to us after nearly three months of continuous fever following a knee replacement surgery. During this period, she had consulted multiple doctors across cities and was treated for common infections like typhoid, malaria and dengue. Despite repeated tests and treatments, the fever persisted, along with joint pain, mouth ulcers and extreme fatigue — without a clear diagnosis.

At SRV Hospitals, under the care of Dr. Avilash Tiwari @dr.avilash_tiwari, the approach shifted from treating symptoms to understanding the full cause. A structured evaluation for long-standing fever was initiated, looking beyond routine infections and considering inflammatory and immune-related conditions.

Advanced testing revealed two key findings. One was a mild, uncommon form of leptospirosis that does not present with the typical severe symptoms and often goes unnoticed. More importantly, investigations confirmed an autoimmune condition called Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), where the immune system becomes overactive and causes ongoing inflammation — leading to persistent fever and joint symptoms.

Very disappointing and disturbing experience at Arihant Multispecialist Hospital

We had a deeply painful and traumatic experience at Arihant Multispecialist Hospital. My nani had already passed away by the afternoon, but the hospital staff unnecessarily prolonged the situation till late night, finally declaring it around 3 AM. This felt extremely inhuman and unethical.

What was even more disturbing is that we witnessed the same thing happening to another patient in front of us. It appeared as though patients were being kept on support despite no real hope, only to delay the inevitable.

If the doctors already knew that my nani would not survive, why were we asked to bring her nighty in the afternoon? Why give false hope and drag the family through hours of emotional torture? This raises serious questions about transparency, ethics, and intentions.

At a time when families are already grieving, such behavior adds unnecessary pain and confusion. Hospitals should prioritize honesty, dignity, and compassion — sadly, we experienced none of these here.

I would strongly urge people to think carefully before choosing this hospital for their loved ones.
